Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexShield Security Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexShield Security's results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Voss, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Ruiz, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Security Officer; Kyle Brennan, VP of Sales; Sophia Grant, Chief Marketing Officer; and Liam Foster, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan: Thank you, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. NexShield Security delivered exceptional results in the Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of NexShield XDR 2.0 is accelerating, demonstrating its transformative impact on threat detection and response, and the unparalleled value we bring to our customers.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: growing the number of customers with ARR over $100K, gathering and acting on customer feedback for new products and features, rolling out recent product and feature launches, improving competitive win rates, maintaining strong net dollar retention rates, driving expansion within existing large accounts, optimizing performance of key product lines like cloud security and SASE, and sustaining robust ARR growth rates both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Rachel Voss to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Rachel Voss: Thank you, David. We achieved record revenue of $1.47 billion in the quarter, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $950 million. Net income was $250 million, resulting in earnings per share of $1.25. We are increasing our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Let me expand on some of these key leading indicators that highlight our enterprise momentum. Starting with our high-value customers—those generating over $100K in annual recurring revenue, or ARR. This group is central to our land-and-expand model in the cybersecurity SaaS space. These accounts not only contribute disproportionately to revenue but also signal the stickiness of our platform and our net revenue retention, or NRR.

At the end of Q3 FY2024, we had 512 such customers, up 25% year-over-year from 410 and 8% sequentially from 474 in Q2. This is our strongest growth in this metric over the past six quarters, surpassing the broader market's 15-18% enterprise expansion rate according to Gartner's latest Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms. These customers now account for 68% of our total ARR, compared to 62% last year, with an average ARR per customer around $285K, thanks to successful upsells and cross-sells into our Zero Trust platform.

NRR for this group stayed at 118%, even with economic pressures, as clients ramp up usage in our SASE offerings, including next-gen firewall-as-a-service and AI-driven UEBA for user and entity behavior analytics. New wins made up 42% of the adds, like a $450K expansion at a top global bank adding our Cloud Workload Protection Platform to their endpoint setup, and our first major hyperscaler deal at $220K ACV for runtime security and container scanning amid supply-chain risks reminiscent of Log4j and SolarWinds.

The other 58% came from upsells, including multi-year renewals exceeding 130% NRR at Fortune 100 industrials in oil and gas, expanding into OT/IoT security against ransomware threats like those hitting critical infrastructure. Our GenAI Threat Hunter launch has powered 35% of these, cutting MTTR by over 40% in trials and integrating with Splunk and Elastic for automated SOAR.

Geographically, North America dominates at 72% of the cohort, up 22% YoY with federal pushes like CMMC 2.0 and the cybersecurity executive order. EMEA jumped 38% to 98 customers via NIS2 and GDPR, with DAX firms taking our DLP for Azure sovereign clouds. APAC grew 55% YoY to 62 customers despite forex hits, led by Japanese finance and Australian infra under new acts.

This validates our platform strategy as the market consolidates. With 95% gross retention and under 1% churn, we're taking share from Check Point and Symantec. We see this reaching 580-600 by year-end, assuming stable macros and no big threat spikes from groups like Lazarus. We're enhancing with Okta identity integrations and ServiceNow orchestration, plus ML deception tech, all while dropping CAC 15% YoY for these logos—true flywheel economics.

Shifting to net dollar retention, or NDR, another pillar of our model. In Q3, we hit 118%, our 11th quarter above 115%, up 300 basis points from Q2's 115% and 6 points from last year. This shows how vital our Nexus platform is as threats intensify. Our Q3 FY2023 cohort now generates 18% more revenue year-over-year through broader adoption.

Gross retention was 98%, with churn at just 1.8%—far below the 5-7% peer average for firms like Palo Alto or Zscaler. Minimal churn hit small mid-market via M&A in finance. Net expansion was 20%, from upsells to AI XDR and CWP. Nexus 4.0's GenAI, blending threat hunting, ZTNA, and SASE, drove 25% ACV growth via ML behavioral analytics against Log4j or LockBit.

Hyperscaler ties fueled 40% of expansions, like AWS and Azure bundles. North America at 62% ARR posted 120% NDR with CISA zero-trust and MDR demand against APT41. EMEA at 116% via GDPR finance expansions; APAC at 110%, up 8 points on ASEAN laws and telco partners; LatAm at 105% improving with our São Paulo center.

This proves our flywheel against point players, with 85% multi-module use creating high switch costs. R&D at 18% targets 125% NDR next year via vertical packs like Healthcare Ransomware Shield.

Next, ARR growth itself. Total ARR reached $528 million, up 12.5% QoQ from $470 million and 48% YoY from $356 million. This beats the market's 14% CAGR and peers amid AI phishing, RaaS, and Change Healthcare-like issues.

New logos gave 42% of QoQ lift with $32 million from 187 customers at $1.7 million average ACV, up 15%. Expansions 35%, retention 23%, DBNRR at 118%. YoY beat CrowdStrike's 33% and Zscaler's 40% via XDR-SASE. ThreatVector acquisition boosted cross-sell.

North America 62% at $328 million, 14% QoQ on hyperscalers. EMEA 16% QoQ to $112 million on GDPR sovereign clouds. APAC 22% QoQ to $74 million on ransomware and SASE. Platform shifts displaced Symantec/Splunk; ShieldAI Sentinel added $18 million; large deals up 28%.

Q4 ARR guidance $565-575 million, 11-13% QoQ. Strong RPO up 52% YoY.

On expansions in large accounts over $1 million ACV, they drove 42% of new ARR, up 15% QoQ. DBNER at 128%, 11th quarter over 120%, beating peer 115%. Expanded 67 accounts, up 29% YoY, average uplift $450K. Base grew 18% to 285, including Fortune 500 finance/healthcare.

61% layered CSPM on EDR amid multi-cloud surge, per Gartner $12 billion forecast. ThreatHunter XDR at 45% attach. U.S. bank example: $2.2M to $3.8M adding ZTNA against credential attacks. Manufacturing via SBOM scanning.

North America 68% at 132% DBNER on CMMC/FedRAMP. EMEA 25% YoY on NIS2 SASE. APAC 10% with 22% uplift on APTs. 98% retention, TAM teams key. Q4 expect 45% contribution, 130% DBNER on ransomware uptick.

Competitive win rates at 68%, up 400 bps QoQ from 64%, 620 bps YoY from 62%—11th straight gain over Gartner's 45% benchmark. Elite vs. CrowdStrike 65-70%, Palo Alto mid-60s.

Vs. Palo Alto 75% (127 deals), 40% TCO edge; telco displaced $15M Prisma. Vs. CrowdStrike 65% (89), GenAI faster MTTR; healthcare post-outage. Microsoft 72% (112) on no-lock-in. Check Point/Fortinet 82% (156) on cloud fit.

Cloud security wins up to 71%. AI/ML PoC to 84%. North America 70%, EMEA 67%, APAC 62%. $450M displacement ACV. Channel 72%, SecureAI investments for 75%+.

Customer feedback on new products has NPS at 78, up from 72, above 55 industry per Gartner. 4,200 enterprises, 85% Fortune 100.

NexShield XDR 2.0: 65% MTTR cut to 12 min, 0.8% false positives via HyperGraph NN. 92% renewals, 45% upsell Autonomous Response. Fortune 500 neutralized supply chain attack fast.

ZeroTrust Edge SASE: 55% mid-market surge, NA 88% Azure/AWS integration. APAC 180% QoQ, telco 99.9% DDoS. QuantumShield beta 95%, Kyber migration.

Iterating GenAI Copilot setup to 72 hours. EMEA DLP 35% on ransomware. LatAm up 25%.

60% Q4 pipeline from feedback, OT/IoT targeting $15B TAM, LTV $4.2M. Voice of Customer predictive.

Key product lines: Cloud Security $248M, 45% YoY, ARR $1.2B, 128% NRR, 22% CNAPP share. Blocked 1.2B events, GenAI MTTR <30 min.

Americas 55%, EMEA 62%, APAC 38%. CSPM convergence, ACV $450K, 82% margins.

SASE $180M, 60% YoY, ARR $850M. 4.5M endpoints, 99.999% uptime, 150 Tbps proxy, 92% ransomware block. Hyperscaler $25M win.

APAC 72% YoY, EMEA 55%, Americas 52%. 65% bundle, 135% NRR, 79% margins. $150M R&D quantum/autonomous.

Recent launches amplifying this: Aegis Shield XDR 2.5 GA August, AegisAI autonomous, 68% MTTR cut, 1,200 logos, $28M ARR, 65% CrowdStrike wins.

Aegis ZeroTrust Edge September, quantum ZTNA, APAC 180% QoQ, 850 enterprises, $15M ARR, 128% NRR.

CloudGuard enhancements: GenAI Shield, IoT/OT DPI. 42% upsell, $12M ARR, 122% expansion. 78% multi-product ARR.

These drive $450M year-end ARR goal.

Dr. Elena Ruiz: Thank you, Rachel. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas include advancing our GenAI integrations for predictive threat emulation and enhancing runtime protections in cloud and SASE environments to stay ahead of zero-days and supply-chain risks.

Marcus Hale: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape—from nation-state APTs to RaaS evolution—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with rigorous FedRAMP and NCSC compliance.

Kyle Brennan: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners and expanding our market share through hyperscaler marketplaces and channel motions.

Sophia Grant: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events. We are also investing in thought leadership initiatives to establish NexShield Security as a trusted advisor in the cybersecurity industry.

Liam Foster: Thank you. Our product strategy focuses on delivering innovative and integrated security solutions that address the evolving needs of our customers. We are constantly gathering feedback from our customers and partners to ensure that our products meet their needs and exceed their expectations, prioritizing platform convergence.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. We'll pause for a moment to assemble the queue. Our first question comes from Mike Patel with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Patel: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Rachel, can you expand on the drivers behind the 118% NDR and how you're seeing expansions play out in large accounts amid longer sales cycles?

Rachel Voss: Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, our 118% NDR reflects the platform's mission-critical role, with gross retention at 98% and 20% net expansion from AI XDR and CWP upsells. In large accounts over $1M ACV, we expanded 67 this quarter, contributing 42% of new ARR at 128% DBNER. Examples include banks adding ZTNA post-credential threats and manufacturing via SBOM tools. Regional strength in North America on compliance helps offset cycles.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Wong: Great results. David, on competitive wins at 68%, how does that break down by product line, especially cloud and SASE versus CrowdStrike and Palo Alto?

David Harlan: Lisa, thanks. That 68% win rate is across the board, with 75% vs. Palo Alto in SASE/NGFW due to TCO and false positive edges, like the EMEA telco displacement. Vs. CrowdStrike in XDR, 65% on faster GenAI MTTR, winning post-outage healthcare. Cloud security at 71%, beating Prisma/Wiz. This drove $450M displacement.

Operator: Next question comes from Tom Reilly with JPMorgan.

Tom Reilly: Solid ARR growth. Elena, with 12.5% QoQ, what tech innovations are fueling the APAC surge, and any risks to guidance?

Dr. Elena Ruiz: Tom, our ShieldAI Sentinel for zero-days and SASE for hybrid work drove APAC's 22% QoQ ARR lift, resonating with ransomware up 37% there. Localized threat intel on Volt Typhoon helped. Guidance holds firm with $4.2B RPO, though we watch geopolitics.

Operator: Next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays.

Sarah Kim: Thanks. Marcus, customer feedback highlights MTTR cuts—how are you addressing setup complexities in new features like GenAI Copilot while monitoring threats?

Marcus Hale: Sarah, feedback drove us to cut Copilot onboarding to 72 hours with no-code tools. MTTR down 65% to 12 minutes in XDR via HyperGraph. We're red-teaming with Mandiant against WormGPT, maintaining vigilance on Clop ransomware and NIS2 compliance.

David Harlan: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Emily Carter: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
